name: Matbench v0.1 glass
description: Predict whether an alloy forms a metallic glass (1) or not (0) from its composition (Matbench v0.1 task glass, 5680 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 200 seconds.
contract: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers, each exactly 0 or 1 (class labels; any other value is invalid). Every input is a dict with the keys formula (a string) and composition (a dict from element symbol to amount). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels (which equals the balanced accuracy), maximized.
notes: Leaderboard best 0.9603 balanced accuracy (MODNet v0.1.12), snapshot of matbench.materialsproject.org read 2026-11-03, date unknown.
matbench_glass.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file
Classifies 5,680 alloy compositions as glass formers (1) or not (0) from the composition alone, scored by ROC AUC on 0/1 labels over the five official folds.
Leaders are graph neural networks and tuned ensembles; the leaderboard snapshot has no date.

The classification score is the ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels, which equals the balanced accuracy: the record is the leaderboard's best balanced accuracy (the page has a second column, probability ROC AUC, that this task does not use).

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify metallic alloy compositions as forming a metallic glass or not (glass-forming ability) from the composition alone.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Metallic glasses combine high strength, elasticity and corrosion resistance, but finding compositions that form glass by experiment is slow and expensive, so predicting glass-forming ability from composition guides alloy discovery.
